openai.sample_unit: patients with AI-detected high likelihood of atrial fibrillation included in the primary analysis
models_evaluated: AI-ECG: 82-layer convolutional neural network for atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter detection

links.outcome: Mortality, ischemic stroke, and bleeding with AI alerts versus usual care
links.effect: All-cause death: HR, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.50–1.04]; no significant ischemic stroke or cardiovascular death differences. Post hoc gastrointestinal bleeding: 2.5% versus 6.9%; HR, 0.35 [95% CI, 0.15–0.85].
links.quote: Regarding secondary end points, the intervention group revealed a numerically lower, but not statistically significant, incidence of all‐cause death (HR, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.50–1.04]) compared with the control group (Figure 3A ).

links.outcome: Off-label anticoagulant prescriptions attributable to false-positive AI-ECG alerts
links.effect: Among 48 intervention and 35 control potential AI errors, only 1 intervention patient received consecutive NOAC prescriptions, justified by subsequent AF; no off-label prescriptions were attributable to AI-ECG errors.
links.quote: As such, there were no instances of off‐label NOAC prescription attributable to potential AI‐ECG errors.

links.outcome: Atrial fibrillation diagnosis by noncardiologists with versus without AI alerts
links.effect: AF diagnosis was 47.8% versus 36.0%; HR, 1.40 [95% CI, 1.03–1.90], favoring clinicians receiving AI-ECG alerts.
links.quote: The diagnosis rates of AF were significantly higher in the intervention group compared with the control group (47.8% versus 36.0%; HR, 1.40 [95% CI, 1.03–1.90]), as depicted in Figure 2 .

links.outcome: Anticoagulant prescribing following immediate physician-phone AI alerts versus no AI alerts
links.effect: NOAC prescription rates within 90 days were 23.3% with alerts versus 12.0% with usual care; HR, 1.85 (95% CI, 1.11–3.07).
links.quote: The prescription rates of NOACs after discharge within 90 days after the index ECG were 23.3% in the intervention group and 12.0% in the control group, resulting in a HR of 1.85 (95% CI, 1.11–3.07).

links.effect: The NOAC prescription rate was significantly higher in the intervention group (23.3%) compared to the control group (12.0%).
links.quote: The non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulant prescription rate was significantly higher in the intervention group (23.3% versus 12.0%; hazard ratio [HR], 1.85 [95% CI, 1.11-3.07]).

links.outcome: clinician failure to act on AI alerts
links.effect: Despite high model accuracy, the misdiagnosis rate among true AF cases remained high at 55.1% in the intervention group.
links.quote: These findings suggest that physicians often did not act on the presence of AF, even when both a formal ECG report and an AI-ECG alert were available, highlighting the need for additional strategies to improve AF recognition and diagnosis.

links.outcome: inappropriate NOAC prescriptions for false positives
links.effect: Zero instances of off-label NOAC prescriptions were caused by potential AI errors among the 48 false positives.
links.quote: As such, there were no instances of off-label NOAC prescription attributable to potential AI-ECG errors.

unlisted_practices: setting AI alert thresholds for high positive predictive value to minimize alert fatigue
automatically excluding patients with clinical contraindications from AI alerts to reduce alert fatigue

screen.practice: AI-ECG alerts to noncardiologist physicians vs usual care
screen.reason: This is a pragmatic cluster randomized controlled trial testing the real-world deployment and clinical impact of AI-ECG alerts sent to noncardiologists compared to usual care.
